BACKPORT: FROMGIT: LSM: generalize flag passing to security_capable This patch provides a general mechanism for passing flags to the security_capable LSM hook. It replaces the specific 'audit' flag that is used to tell security_capable whether it should log an audit message for the given capability check. The reason for generalizing this flag passing is so we can add an additional flag that signifies whether security_capable is being called by a setid syscall (which is needed by the proposed SafeSetID LSM). Reason for BACKPORT label: aa_capable() function in security/apparmor/capability.c had slightly different logical operator in 4.14. vs latest upstream code. There is no logical difference between the two. Also, change code in security/chromiumos/lsm.c to take advantage of opts arg in security_capable. This allows to refrain from checking the current syscall number when seeing if security_capable is being called from a setid syscall in the chromiumos LSM. Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.morris@microsoft.com> (cherry picked from commit c1a85a00ea66cb6f0bd0f14e47c28c2b0999799f git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/jmorris/linux-security.git origin/next-general) Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:845640 TEST=Kernel selftest that I wrote for this LSM Change-Id: Ib004f250a7dd0328eef5cc4fdf0652c3d588a987 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1460039 Commit-Ready: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Tested-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: LSM: add SafeSetID module that gates setid calls This change ensures that the set*uid family of syscalls in kernel/sys.c (setreuid, setuid, setresuid, setfsuid) all call ns_capable_common with the CAP_OPT_INSETID flag, so capability checks in the security_capable hook can know whether they are being called from within a set*uid syscall. This change is a no-op by itself, but is needed for the proposed SafeSetID LSM. Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Acked-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.morris@microsoft.com> (cherry picked from commit 40852275a94afb3e836be9248399e036982d1a79 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/jmorris/linux-security.git origin/next-general) Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:845640 TEST=Kernel selftest that I wrote for this LSM Change-Id: I35c3f45394ff936f1db01ee6885d01c7ddb5dc85 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1464481 Commit-Ready: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Tested-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: FROMGIT: LSM: add SafeSetID module that gates setid calls SafeSetID gates the setid family of syscalls to restrict UID/GID transitions from a given UID/GID to only those approved by a system-wide whitelist. These restrictions also prohibit the given UIDs/GIDs from obtaining auxiliary privileges associated with CAP_SET{U/G}ID, such as allowing a user to set up user namespace UID mappings. For now, only gating the set*uid family of syscalls is supported, with support for set*gid coming in a future patch set. Reason for BACKPORT label: defining/registering an LSM is slightly different in 4.14 than it is in the latest upstream code. Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Acked-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: James Morris <james.morris@microsoft.com> (cherry picked from commit aeca4e2ca65c1aeacfbe520684e6421719d99417 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/jmorris/linux-security.git origin/next-general) Signed-off-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:845640 TEST=Kernel selftest that I wrote for this LSM Change-Id: Ia79d33f0ef97cfc63335f8b85fcde14dfb3d908d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1460040 Commit-Ready: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Tested-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

motion_sense: send ODR events to the AP This commits enables the EC to send a motion sense event to the AP when a sensor's ODR is changed. This is done in a way that is backwards compatible on the AP side, in order to enable previous kernels to continue to work (albeit at a loss of new functionality) with up-to-date ECs. Since clients are not required to use a FLUSH when changing ODR, it is possible for the sensor ring to get in a state where it is spreading based on out-of-date delay information, which we observed leading to spreading of overly large intervals, and thus too far into the future. This patch ameliorates that by causing an ODR change to implicitly flush the batching history. crosvm: use seqpacket rather than datagram sockets The advantage of seqpacket is that they are connection oriented. A listener can be created that accepts new connections, useful for the path based VM control sockets. Previously, the only bidirectional sockets in crosvm were either stream based or made using socketpair. This change also whitelists sendmsg and recvmsg for the common device policy. BACKPORT: vhost/vsock: fix use-after-free in network stack callers If the network stack calls .send_pkt()/.cancel_pkt() during .release(), a struct vhost_vsock use-after-free is possible. This occurs because .release() does not wait for other CPUs to stop using struct vhost_vsock. Switch to an RCU-enabled hashtable (indexed by guest CID) so that .release() can wait for other CPUs by calling synchronize_rcu(). This also eliminates vhost_vsock_lock acquisition in the data path so it could have a positive effect on performance. This is CVE-2018-14625 "kernel: use-after-free Read in vhost_transport_send_pkt". BUG=b:116967828 TEST=Syzkaller PoC Backport Note : * Use DEFINE_HASHTABLE instead of DEFINE_READ_MOSTLY_HASHTABLE * Changes to vhost_transport_cancel_pkt have been ommited in this CL as vhost_transport_cancel_pkt() is not present in chromeos-4.4. npcx: pwm: Turn off pwm signal by setting DCRn greater than CTRn. In npcx pwm modules, there're two ways to turn off pwm signal. One is clearing PWR bit in PWMCTL. The other is setting DCRn's value greater than CTRn's. The current pwm driver adopts the first method. But we saw pwm signal doesn't be turned off by the following sequence: 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); Please notice setting zero in DCRn doesn't mean duty cycle is zero. (NPCX duty cycle: ( (DCRn+1) / (CTRn+1) ) x 100). Hence in step 2, we can observe a very low duty cycle once the driver enabled pwm module. This CL adopts the second method to turn off pwm module. In order to make sure DCRn can be greater than CTRn, we also defined the PWN maximum duty cycle is (0xFFFF -1) since both DCR and CTR are 16-bits registers. BRANCH=none BUG=b:123552920 TEST=No build errors for npcx5/7 series. Test pwm console command on npcx5/7 evbs by the following sequence. 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); And no symptoms are observed. PWM_CONFIG_ACTIVE_LOW flag is tested also and no symptom occurred. Change-Id: I92517ff0bf3e027ae191be00112cd71ec4b55a2b Signed-off-by: Mulin Chao <mlchao@nuvoton.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1475096 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
